question: A rectangular grid maze has 1481 rows and 1480 columns of unit squares. For each middle row (that is, rows 2 through 1480), there is exactly one invisible teleportation gate hidden in that row, and all of these gates lie in one of the same two columns. An explorer may start each attempt from any chosen square in the top row. In an attempt, the explorer may move one square at a time up, down, left, or right, revisiting squares if desired. If the explorer steps on a teleportation gate, the attempt immediately ends and the explorer is returned to the starting square of that attempt; the exact gate location just triggered is then recorded and remembered for future attempts. If the explorer reaches any square in the bottom row, they immediately succeed and the process stops. What is the minimum possible value of k such that a strategy can guarantee success by the k-th attempt, no matter how the gates are placed subject to the rules?

In a math contest, for each integer n ≥ 5, define an (n − 5 + 1) by (n − 5 + 1) matrix M_n(λ) as follows: for i = 5, 5 + 1, …, n, the i-th diagonal entry is (i + 4)(i + 4 + 1)…(i + 4 + 5 − 1) − λ, and every off-diagonal entry equals −λ. Let λ_n be the maximal real λ > 0 with det(M_n(λ)) = 0. Determine the exact value of L = limsup_{n→∞} λ_n.

Define N to be the least positive integer that cannot be expressed as a sum of at most 1767 terms of the form ± 2^{b_i}, where each b_i is a nonnegative integer and repetitions of exponents are allowed. Compute N modulo 61713647.

On an 9x8 grid, a bishop moves along diagonals, but blocked squares stop lines of sight and cannot be occupied. Let B be the set of blocked squares, listed as row-column pairs with 1-based indices: [(1, 7), (2, 8), (3, 2), (3, 3), (3, 7), (3, 8), (4, 1), (4, 4), (5, 8), (6, 8), (7, 3), (7, 4), (8, 6), (9, 6)].
You may mark only unblocked squares. Determine the smallest number of unblocked squares that must be marked so that for every legal placement of a single bishop on any unblocked square, each of the two diagonals through that square contains at least one marked unblocked square (the bishop's own square counts if it is marked). Provide only the minimal number.

In a cyclic arrangement of 9 positive integers x_1, x_2, ..., x_9 (indices taken modulo 9), and for an exponent p = 5, let D be the set of offsets 2, 3, 4 with corresponding positive integer weights given by 2:2, 3:4, 4:3. Determine the largest real constant C such that for all choices of the x_i,

  (x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_9)^5 >= C * gcd(x_1, x_2, ..., x_9)^{p-2} * sum_{d in D} w_d * sum_{i=1}^9 (gcd(x_i, x_{i+d}) * lcm(x_{i+d}, x_i)).

Here w_d denotes the weight associated with offset d, and the sums are taken with indices modulo 9.

On an n×n grid, you must place exactly 13240 coins so that each cell holds an integer number of coins between 0 and 65, inclusive. For any two squares sharing a side, the absolute difference in their coin counts must be exactly 2 if the squares are horizontally adjacent and exactly 1 if the squares are vertically adjacent. Determine the largest possible n for which such an arrangement exists.

In a math contest, 11 distinct positive integers are to be arranged around a circle, using each integer from the multiset [58,20,50,18,56,15,80,55,16,19,43] exactly once. For a cyclic ordering a_1, a_2, ..., a_11 (with a_{m+1} = a_1), define S = \sum_{i=1}^11 \left\lfloor \frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i} \right\rfloor. Determine the minimal possible value of S over all such cyclic orderings.

On a cylindrical chessboard with 5 rows and 14 columns (rows wrap top-to-bottom, columns do not), a king attacks any piece in one of the eight neighboring squares (sharing a side or a vertex). Determine the maximum number of kings that can be placed so that each king attacks exactly one other king, and no king attacks any non-partner. Give the value of this maximum for the specified 5 and 14.

In a two-stage dice game, 4 fair 6-sided dice are rolled. After observing the outcomes, you must choose exactly 3 of the dice to re-roll once; the remaining dice are kept. Let p be the maximal probability (over all outcome-dependent choices of which 3 dice to re-roll) that the final sum of all dice equals 16. Compute 279936 * p.

Let n = 13 be a fixed positive integer. Determine the largest positive integer m for which there exist pairwise distinct, nonzero complex numbers r_1, r_2, ..., r_13 with the property that for every integer j satisfying 1 ≤ j ≤ m and for every s in the set {1, 2, ..., 13}, the product ∏_{k=1}^{13} (r_k^(s j) + 1) is equal to 1. Report the remainder when this maximal m is divided by 7842425.

On a toroidal chessboard with wrap-around edges (top connects to bottom, left connects to right), consider a 35×35 grid of unit squares. We place n pieces on distinct squares. For each piece, define its range to be the axis-aligned 9×9 square centered at the piece, interpreted on the torus, so that the range consists of all squares whose Chebyshev (L∞) distance on the torus from the piece is at most 4. Suppose that the range of each piece contains exactly one other piece (no more, no less). What is the maximum possible n?
Consider the sequence {a_n} defined by a_1 = 19/(19^2+1) and, for all n ≥ 1, by the relation a_n^2 = a_{n+1} − 2 a_n^2 a_{n+1}. Compute the residue of floor(1/a_{327}) modulo 69647.
Let (a_n) be a real sequence defined for all integers n >= 0 by a_{n+1} = (1 n + 1) 4^{n} - 8 a_n. Determine the minimal possible value of 1/a_0 such that a_{n+1} > a_n holds for every n >= 0.

Consider the following hyperplane arrangement in R^6. There are exactly 6 axis-parallel families: for each i in {1,...,6}, the family consists of all hyperplanes of the form x_i = constant, with the family sizes given (in order i = 1 to i = 6) by 3, 3, 2, 5, 3, 3. In addition, there are 4 oblique families of hyperplanes whose normals are mutually non-parallel and not parallel to any coordinate axis, with respective family sizes 3, 4, 2, 1. Assume general position in the following precise sense: within any selection of at most 6 distinct families, the set of normal directions is linearly independent; within each family all hyperplanes are distinct and parallel; and no point of R^6 lies on hyperplanes from 7 or more distinct families. Under these hypotheses, how many regions does this entire collection of hyperplanes partition R^6 into? Give your answer as an integer.

Let R be the planar region defined by min{|x - 6|, |x + 6|} + 2|y| ≤ 4. Consider the image set S = { (3y - 4) / (-2x - 2) : (x, y) ∈ R }. Assume S has finite total length (its Lebesgue measure on the real line), and write this total length as m/p in lowest terms. Find m + p.

In three-dimensional space, let ABCD be an isosceles trapezoid inscribed in a sphere with center O, where AB ∥ CD, AB = 4, CD = 6, and AD = BC = 5.0990195135927845. Points E and F vary on segments AD and BC, respectively. It is known that the minimum possible value of the dot product of vectors OE and OF over all such choices of E and F equals -10. Determine the least integer that is greater than the volume of the sphere.

Consider circular necklaces with 14 positions colored using exactly 3 colors. Two necklaces are considered equivalent if one is a rotation of the other (reflections are not allowed). No color may appear in a run of 5 or more consecutive beads anywhere around the circle. Additionally, the necklace must use at least 3 distinct colors. How many such rotation-equivalence classes are there?

In the infinite unit square lattice (checkerboard) of grid spacing 1, a rectangle with side lengths 19/12 and 8/9 is dropped onto the plane with its center uniformly distributed modulo the lattice and its orientation chosen uniformly at random and independently of its position. Let p be the probability that this rectangle does not cover any lattice vertex. Compute floor(1000 * p).

Let x_1 <= x_2 <= ... <= x_60 be real numbers with x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_60 = 1. Set m = 30 and define
Q = ((sum_{i=1}^{60} |x_i - x_30| + sum_{i=1}^{60} |x_i - x_31|)^2 * sum_{1 <= i < j <= 60} (x_i - x_j)^2) / (sum_{i=1}^{60} x_i^2)^3.
Find the maximum possible value of Q.

In a rectangular grid of 33 by 32 unit squares, some squares are selected. In each selected square, you must draw exactly one directed unit segment, chosen to be either the top edge oriented from its top-left corner to its top-right corner (an east arrow) or the right edge oriented from its bottom-right corner to its top-right corner (a north arrow). The constraint is that for any two drawn segments, unless the endpoint (head) of one coincides with the starting point (tail) of the other, both the Euclidean distance between their endpoints and the Euclidean distance between their starting points are at least 2. Determine the maximum possible number of selected squares.

On a 2771×460 chessboard, a generalized diagonal is a set of squares with no two in the same row or column. Some squares are colored red so that every row has at most 122 red squares and every column has at most 94 red squares. Determine the minimum positive integer n such that for any such coloring, it is always possible to find n generalized diagonals whose union contains all red squares, under the extra constraint that each diagonal contains at most 240 squares.

Let (a_n)_{n>=1} be an infinite sequence of positive integers with a_1 = 1. Fix two integers 2 >= 2 and 6279 >= 2. Assume the following strengthened sliding-sum divisibility holds simultaneously for two coprime window families: for every positive integer n and every integer k >= 1 we have both (i) a_n divides a_k + a_{k+1} + ... + a_{k+n-1}, and (ii) a_n divides a_k + a_{k+2} + ... + a_{k+(n-1)2} (the sum of n terms with step 2). Let N be the maximal possible value of a_6279 among all such sequences. Compute N modulo 17792.

Let a1(n) = n^2 - 20 n + 173, a2(n) = n^2 - (20 - 1) n + (173 + 24), and a3(n) = n^2 - (20 + 2) n + (173 + 26). Consider all integers n with |n| ≤ 43 for which a1(n), a2(n), and a3(n) are all prime numbers (primes are taken to be positive integers greater than 1). Among those n, further require that S(n) = a1(n) + a2(n) + a3(n) is a perfect square. Compute the sum of all distinct values of S(n) over all such n.

In a math contest, a frog starts at 0 and must visit each integer in the set {1, 2, ..., {up_to}} exactly once, in any order. Every jump has length 2^k for some k in {0, 1, ..., 11}, and the direction may be left or right. A cost profile assigns a weight c_k to each allowed jump length 2^k. The total penalty of a route is the sum, over all jumps, of c_k / 2^k for each jump of length 2^k. Given n = 12 and the cost profile (c_0, c_1, ..., c_11) = (6,3,6,5,2,7,2,7,7,9,8,3), determine the minimum possible total penalty over all valid routes.

Consider a convex polygon with 55 labeled vertices, triangulated by drawing all diagonals from vertex 1 to the other nonadjacent vertices. This produces 53 triangular faces and 107 edges. Each edge is painted in one of 22 colors, of which exactly 12 are designated heavy. For every triangular face, the three edge colors must use exactly two distinct colors, and moreover the color that appears twice on that face must be one of the heavy colors. How many edge-colorings satisfy these conditions? Give your answer modulo 1000000009.

Fix an odd prime 977. Only odd common differences up to 7 are admissible. Consider all positive integers N that can be written as a sum of k consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression with common difference d from the admissible set, for exactly one ordered pair (k, d) with k > 1; furthermore, that unique representation must have length k = 977. Among all such N, determine the minimal possible starting term a of that unique representation.

Let a, b, c be nonnegative real numbers with a + b + c = 9. For the fixed integers p = 6 (with p >= 2), q = 1 (with q >= 1), and r = 1 (with r >= 1), consider the expression F(a, b, c) = (a^p + b^p + c^p) / ((ab + bc + ca)^q * ((a + b)(b + c)(c + a))^r). Determine the minimum value of F(a, b, c). Express your answer as a reduced fraction m/n, and then compute m + n.

In Euclidean 8-space, 13 points are chosen independently and uniformly at random inside the unit ball centered at the origin. Let p be the probability that the origin lies outside the convex hull of these points. Writing p in lowest terms as m/n, determine the value of n - m.

A coin has an unknown heads probability p with prior Beta(3, 1), i.e., a density proportional to p^{alpha-1}(1-p)^{beta-1} on [0,1]. Conditional on p, the coin is tossed in 5 independent blocks, each block consisting of 6 tosses. Let X be the number of blocks that produce exactly 2 heads. Compute the unconditional probability P(X = 2). Express your answer as a reduced fraction m/n and report m+n.

Consider a function g: N×N → N with g(0,0)=0. Fix integers 4 and 15 with 1 ≤ p < q. For every x,y ≥ 0, both conditions hold:
- The four corner values of the unit square satisfy {g(x,y), g(x+1,y), g(x,y+1), g(x+1,y+1)} = {n, n+4, n+15, n+4+15} for some integer n depending on (x,y).
- The edge increments are monotone and constrained by g(x+1,y) − g(x,y) ∈ { 4, 15 } and g(x,y+1) − g(x,y) ∈ { 4, 15 }.
Let S be the set of all possible values of g(53,95) over all functions g satisfying the above. Determine the 2-th smallest value of S.

On a circle with 14 equally spaced points, the balls labeled 1, 2, ..., 14 are randomly placed with one ball per point. Two placements that can be matched by a rotation or a reflection are considered the same. Let S be the sum of the absolute differences of the labels on all adjacent pairs around the circle. Let the shorter cyclic distance between labels 1 and 14 be the number of edges along the shorter arc connecting them; call this distance exactly 2. What is the reciprocal of the probability that, for a uniformly random placement (modulo rotation and reflection), S attains its minimum possible value and, simultaneously, the shorter cyclic distance between 1 and 14 equals 2?

Let n be a positive integer and let its positive divisors be ordered as d1 < d2 < ... < dl. Fix an odd integer 17 that is both a sum of two squares and a nontrivial difference of two squares. Find the minimal value of n such that all of the following hold simultaneously: (1) d_13 = 17; (2) there exist indices i < j with d_i^2 + d_j^2 = d_13^2 and gcd(d_i, d_j) = 1 (so d_13 is the hypotenuse of a primitive Pythagorean triple among the divisors of n); (3) there exist indices p, q with d_13^2 + d_p^2 = d_q^2 and gcd(d_13, d_p) = 1 (so d_13 is the odd leg of a primitive Pythagorean triple among the divisors of n).

You are allowed to pick three disjoint sets of distinct positive integers. For the first set, pick exactly a integers that are each congruent to 1 modulo 5 and all at least 16. For the second, pick exactly b integers that are each congruent to 2 modulo 5 and all at least 27. For the third, pick exactly c integers that are each congruent to 4 modulo 5 and all at least 14. All picked integers across the three sets must be pairwise distinct, and their total sum must be exactly 4231. Among all triples (a, b, c) for which such selections are possible, determine the maximum value of 17a + 15b + 4c.

You are given the vertices of a convex 131769-gon in the plane. The only tool available is a device that, for any two constructed points P and Q, places all m−1 interior points that divide the segment PQ into m equal parts. You may apply this operation repeatedly, but you restrict yourself to constructions in which every constructed point is an affine combination of the original vertices whose coefficients have denominator at most m to the power 2. For how many integers m in the interval [613, 147456] can you necessarily construct the centroid of the 131769 vertices under this restriction?

Fix an odd prime 11. For each positive integer n, let L_p(n) be the last non-zero digit of n! when written in base 11. Let k_p(t) be the 10-th smallest positive integer k such that L_p(k n) = L_p(n) for all integers n ≥ 1. For the given 11 and 10, how many base-10 digits does k_p(t) have?

Let S = {1, 2, ..., 78} and list its 2^78 subsets as A_1, A_2, ..., A_{2^78}. For any two subsets, define the symmetric difference A_i Δ A_j. For each ordered pair (i, j), compute z_{i,j} = sum_{x in A_i Δ A_j} (4·x + 13), where the sum over an empty set is 0, and fill the table entry M_{i,j} = 2·z_{i,j}^2 + 3·z_{i,j} + 7. Let T be the sum of all entries M_{i,j} taken only over those pairs with |A_i Δ A_j| ≡ 1 (mod 4). Find the remainder of T when divided by 55203701.

In a math contest, 7 real numbers x_1, x_2, ..., x_7 satisfy |x_1| + |x_2| + ... + |x_7| = 1. Let (c_2, c_3, ..., c_7) = (5, 4, 3, 2, 4, 4), and define
D = |x_1| + \sum_{k=2}^{7} |c_k(x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_{k-1}) - x_k|.
Let M be the maximal possible value of 1/D over all such real sequences (x_i). Compute M modulo 939.

You are given n = 5. Consider real vector x = (x_1, ..., x_n) satisfying sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i^2 = 1, and a strictly positive vector y = (y_1, ..., y_n) with sum_{i=1}^n a_i y_i = 18.13322558634304. Here the positive weights are c_i listed as [1, 1, 3, 5, 5] and a_i listed as [4, 2, 2, 2, 5]. Let d be the minimal possible value of max_i |y_i - x_i| over all feasible x and y. Determine the largest integer less than 1600 * d.

In a math contest, 10 students are to be analyzed via a symmetric 10×10 binary matrix A (entries 0 or 1) with zero diagonal. Each row of A has exactly 8 ones. Additionally, A satisfies the spectral identity A^2 + 2·A = a matrix whose every entry equals 8. Under these conditions, determine the number of such matrices A. (Equivalently, count the number of ways the 10 labeled students can be split into 5 equally-sized hidden teams of size 2 so that edges connect students from different teams only, consistent with the matrix equation above.)

Let F_115063617043 be the finite field with q=115063617043 elements, where q=163^{ {m} }. Define W to be the smallest set of polynomials with coefficients in F_115063617043 satisfying all of the following: (i) the m translation polynomials x+t_1, x+t_2, ..., x+t_m are in W, where t_1, ..., t_m form an F_163-basis of F_115063617043; (ii) for each of r=3 indices i among {1,2,...,m}, the unique degree-<q polynomial over F_115063617043 that, as a function on F_115063617043, swaps a and a+t_i (for a fixed but arbitrary a in F_115063617043) and fixes every other field element is in W; (iii) whenever h_1,h_2 are in W, the remainder of h_1(h_2(x)) modulo x^115063617043-x is also in W. Let N be the number of distinct polynomials in W modulo x^115063617043-x. How many consecutive zeros are there at the end of the base-1470000 representation of N?

For each real x in [0,1), define f(x) = sum_{n=1}^∞ 2^{-n} over those n for which floor(n x + 6/7) modulo 7 lies in the residue set [[0, 1, 3, 4, 5]]. Let L_max be the largest real number such that f(x) ≥ L for all x ∈ [0,1). Determine the largest integer strictly less than 1000 · L_max.

Consider ordered integer pairs (a, b) satisfying a^2 + 2 b^2 ≤ 168. Suppose there exist positive real numbers x and y such that a/√x + 5/(y + 5 x) = 1 and b/√y − 5/(y + 5 x) = 1. Let N be the number of such ordered pairs (a, b). Compute N^2.

Let 9 be a fixed integer and let s = 17/12 be a rational number with 0 < s < 2. Determine the minimal integer C such that for every positive integer n and all real numbers x_0, x_1, ..., x_n, the inequality

Sum_{0 ≤ i,j ≤ n} 9^{i+j+1} * binom(i+j, i) * x_i * x_j + Sum_{0 ≤ i ≤ n} (9 * 17/12)^i * x_i ≥ - C / 8489

holds.

In a math contest, 47 distinct positive integers \(a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{47}\) have total sum 3331. For \(1\le k\le 46\), define
\[
b_k=\min(a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_k,\ a_{k+1}+a_{k+2}+\cdots+a_{47}).
\]
Let \(S\) be the maximum of \(b_k\) over all such \(k\). Among all valid sequences \((a_i)\), determine the minimal possible value of \(S\).

In a math contest, a 502×502 number table must be filled with the integers 1, 2, ..., 252004, each used exactly once. For every pair of numbers that lie in the same row or the same column, take the ratio of the larger to the smaller. The smallest of all these ratios is called the characteristic value of the table. Among all possible such fillings, let the maximum possible characteristic value be λ = α/β in lowest terms. Compute α + β.

In a math contest, consider all integers k in the interval [2, 3226]. For fixed parameters r = 2 and modulus m = 5, call a triple (n, a, b) admissible if: n is odd and has exactly r distinct prime factors; each prime factor of n is congruent to 1 modulo m and also divides k; gcd(a, b) = 1; a + b = k; and n divides a^n + b^n. How many integers k in [2, 3226] make the set of admissible triples finite?

On a circle of radius 1/12, a regular 20-gon is inscribed. The polygon is rotated so that one vertex lies at an angle of 1.626215 degrees from the positive x-axis. Let E and F be points on the circle such that the central angle ∠EOF equals 2×(223/6) degrees, and the midpoint direction of arc EF is aligned with the positive x-axis. For a point M ranging over all points on the edges (line segments) of the polygon, define S as the minimum possible value of the Euclidean dot product between vectors MF and ME. Compute the value of ceil(35566 × (−S)).

Let 136 be a fixed positive integer with 136 >= 6. For any non-empty finite subset S of {1,2,...,136}, define the weighted mean f_w(S) = (sum_{x in S} x^2) / (sum_{x in S} x). Consider all ordered pairs (A, B) of disjoint non-empty subsets with A ∪ B = {1, 2, ..., 136}, 1 ≤ |A| ≤ 136-2, and 2 ≤ |B| ≤ 136-1. For any p in B, define A_p = A ∪ {p} and B_p = B \ {p}. Over all choices of (A, B) satisfying the conditions and all p in B, determine the maximum possible value of (f_w(A_p) − f_w(A)) · (f_w(B_p) − f_w(B)). If the maximum can be expressed as an irreducible fraction u/v, report u + v.

Consider a regular 5-simplex with side length 7/4. A rigid ball moves freely inside it. The center of the ball must remain at least c_i times the inradius of the simplex away (perpendicularly) from the i-th face F_i, for each i = 1, 2, ..., 5+1, where the multipliers (c_1, ..., c_{dimension+1}) are given by 5/7, 1/8, 3/8, 1/5, 1/4, 5/8. Let V be the 5-dimensional volume of the set of all reachable positions of the center. Compute floor(1 / V^2).

In a math contest, the committee fixes an exponent 270. Determine the minimal positive integer n ≥ 306 for which there exists a bijection f: {1, ..., n} → {1, ..., n} satisfying both of the following for all x, y in {1, ..., n}: (i) If n divides 270·x − y, then n+1 divides f(x)^{ 270 } − f(y). (ii) If n divides x + y, then n+1 divides f(x)·f(y) − 1. Find n.

In a math contest, let n = 892 and k = 3. For each integer i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, define f(i) = i^k / (i^k + (n − i)^k). Let D be the following set of positive divisors of n: 1, 2, 4, 223. For each d in D, assign an even weight w(d) as follows: 1:6, 2:10, 4:12, 223:8. Consider the weighted sum T = sum over all integers i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 and gcd(i, n) ∈ D of w(gcd(i, n)) · f(i). Compute the exact value of T.

In a math contest, non-negative reals x, y, z satisfy 12x^2 + 10y^2 + 2z^2 = 1. For each i = 1, ..., 6, define f_i as the maximal value of 4(p_i·xy + q_i·xz) under this constraint. The sequences (p_i), (q_i), and weights (w_i) are given respectively by 9, 7, 7, 9, 2, 5, 8, 6, 3, 2, 4, 3, and 2, 11, 12, 8, 1, 4. Find the largest integer no more than S = \sum_{i=1}^6 w_i f_i^2.

Let I_n(a,k,q)=∫_0^{π/q} [sin^2(nt)]/[sin t + a·sin(kt)] dt, where a, k, q are positive integers and k is odd. Compute ⌊2226 · lim_{n→∞} (I_n(a,k,q)/log_2 n)⌋ for the specific parameters a=3, k=5, q=8.

In a math contest, 3 students are assigned positive real weights x_1, ..., x_3. Let S = x_1 + ... + x_3. Fix rational parameters r = 2/3 with 0 < r < 1 and c = 23/10. Determine the minimal integer k such that, for all choices of positive x_i, the inequality sum_{i=1}^3 x_i / (x_i + c S)^{r} ≤ (k / 2000) * S^{1 - r} holds.

In a math contest, 2313 students each hold one cookie of every one of 69 distinct shapes. For every student i there is a single preferred shape p_i. The mass of the cookie of that preferred shape is h, while the mass of each of the other 69 − 1 cookies is the same value l = 1/1359. All students share the same h and l, with h and l positive and satisfying h + (69 − 1)·l = 1 and h > l. You must select exactly one cookie from each student. If a student is assigned to their preferred shape, that student contributes mass h to that shape’s total; if assigned to any non-preferred shape, they contribute mass l to that shape’s total.

Let C be the smallest positive real number such that, no matter how the preferred shapes p_i are arranged among the 69 shapes, it is always possible to select one cookie from each student so that, for every shape, the total mass of the selected cookies of that shape does not exceed C. Write C in simplest fractional form q/p and report p + q.

Let S = {1,2,...,2960} and define the reflection map φ(x) = 2960+1 - x. Fix 4, a power of two. Let M be the number of bijections f: S → S such that for every a ∈ S, one has f^[4](a) + f^[-4](a) = 2960+1, where f^[k] denotes the k-fold iterate of f (and f^[-k] = (f^{-1})^[k]). Determine the largest integer k such that 2^k divides M.

In a math contest, 147 real numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_147 satisfy the cyclic Lipschitz condition |a_i - a_{i+1}| ≤ 1 for all 1 ≤ i ≤ 147, where a_{148} := a_1, and the global sum constraint a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_147 = 3. Let p = 25 and m = ⌊147/p⌋ = 5, and consider the arithmetic progression of indices {p, 2p, 3p, ..., mp} = {25, 50, 75, 100, 125}. Define F = a_p + a_{2p} + ... + a_{mp} = a_25 + a_50 + a_75 + a_100 + a_125. Determine the maximum possible value of F, rounded to 10 decimal places.

Consider a cyclic sequence of 5587 real numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_5587. Fix a step size 774 with 1 <= 774 < 5587, and interpret indices modulo 5587. Define the set of pair-sums S_774 = { |a_i + a_{i+774}| : i = 1, 2, ..., 5587 }. Determine the smallest positive integer t such that for every choice of the reals a_1, ..., a_5587, the inequality max_{1 <= i <= 5587} |a_i| <= t * max S_774 always holds.

Let 2979 and 2259 be positive integers. Consider two sequences of positive real numbers x_1, x_2, ..., x_2979 and y_1, y_2, ..., y_2259. Define M to be the minimal possible value of max{x_1, 1/x_1 + x_2, 1/x_2 + x_3, ..., 1/x_{n-1} + x_2979, 1/x_2979 + 1}, and define N similarly for the y-sequence: N is the minimal possible value of max{y_1, 1/y_1 + y_2, ..., 1/y_{m-1} + y_2259, 1/y_2259 + 1}. Suppose a monic self-reciprocal polynomial F(x) with integer coefficients is divisible by both quadratics x^2 - M x + 1 and x^2 - N x + 1. Determine the minimal possible degree of F(x).

On a circular table with 73 seats arranged in a cycle, the integers 1, 2, ..., 73 are placed one per seat. Two seats are considered adjacent if they are next to each other on the circle. Let S be a real number such that, for every pair of adjacent seats, the sum of the two integers written on them is at least S. Determine, in terms of 73, the maximum possible value of S under an optimal arrangement.

Consider all complex roots $z$ (counting multiplicity) of the equation
\[
z^{101}+14z^{100}+6=0.
\]
How many of these roots are non-real and lie strictly inside the unit circle $|z|<1$?

Let P(x) and Q(x) be distinct real polynomials of degree 554 whose coefficients of x^0, x^1, ..., x^554 are all nonzero. Let r be the total multiplicity of their common real roots, and let s be the number of indices j in {0,1,...,554} for which the coefficient of x^j in P equals the coefficient of x^j in Q. Determine the maximum possible value of r + s.

A regular 11-gon is partitioned into 11 labeled sectors 1,2,...,11 around its center. You have 5 available colors labeled 1 through 5, and you must color each sector with exactly one color, subject to these constraints:
1) Cyclic distance constraint: any two sectors whose circular index distance is at most 2 must have different colors.
2) Adjacent-pair ban: for adjacent sectors (distance 1), none of the unordered color pairs in (2,4) may appear on the two sectors (in either order). Pairs not listed are allowed provided the colors are distinct.
3) Exactly 4 distinct colors must be used overall.
4) The color of sector 1 is fixed to be 5.
All colorings are counted as distinct (no symmetry quotienting). How many valid colorings are there?

In a math contest, 181 observers stand at the vertices of a regular 181-gon inscribed in a circle. For each observer i, you may choose a clockwise viewing angle theta_i (in degrees), with 0 <= theta_i <= 175. The viewing sector for observer i is a wedge of angle theta_i whose bisector is aligned with the clockwise tangent at i; observer i sees exactly those other vertices lying strictly within that clockwise arc (including points exactly on the wedge boundaries). Let a_i be the number of other observers seen by observer i. Subject to the global budget constraint sum_{i=1}^181 theta_i <= 7344, determine the maximum possible value of sum_{i=1}^181 a_i.

On a cyclic board labeled 1 through 46, define the relation x ≻_{t} y to mean the clockwise modular distance from y to x (taken modulo 46) lies in {1,2,...,t}. Given an integer 5 and a threshold vector [17, 35, 17, 32, 38] = (t_1, t_2, ..., t_5), count the number of k-tuples (x_1, x_2, ..., x_5) with each x_i in {1,2,...,46} such that for every i = 1, 2, ..., 5-1, x_i ≻_{t_list[i-1]} x_{i+1}, and also x_5 ≻_{t_list[5-1]} x_{1}. Return the exact integer count.
In a math contest, 2296 real numbers x_1,...,x_2296 are chosen so that each lies in [-8,3] and x_1+...+x_2296 = -14072. Determine the exact maximum possible value of x_1^8 + x_2^8 + ... + x_2296^8.

A rectangle is subdivided by drawing some number of full-length vertical lines and some number of full-length horizontal lines, all parallel to the rectangle's sides, producing a rectangular grid with exactly 1428 small rectangles (i.e., there exist nonnegative integers v,h with (v+1)(h+1)=1428). Nodes are the grid intersections and fundamental line segments are the minimal side segments of the grid between consecutive nodes. Let H be the number of horizontal fundamental segments and V be the number of vertical fundamental segments. For given positive integers 9 and 5, define W = 9·H + 5·V. Among all such grid subdivisions producing exactly 1428 small rectangles, determine the sum of the maximum possible value of W and the minimum possible value of W.

On a square grid with 18 rows and 18 columns, you place black stones on some cells. Determine the minimum number of stones needed to guarantee that every axis-parallel 6×6 square subgrid contains at least one black stone. Equivalently, there is no 6×6 contiguous empty block anywhere on the board. Give your answer as an integer.

Let G be a simple graph on 272 vertices. For every vertex u, there exists a neighbor v such that u and v have no common neighbors (i.e., N(u) ∩ N(v) = ∅). In addition, require that the collection of such "witness" edges can be chosen to be pairwise vertex-disjoint (so there is a matching M consisting entirely of triangle-free edges, and every vertex is incident to some edge in M). Among all such graphs, determine the maximal possible number of edges.

In a math contest, 59 numbered seats are arranged around a circular table. A subset S of these seats is called admissible if |S| = 16 and, in every block of 6 consecutive seats around the circle, at most 5 of them lie in S. How many admissible subsets are there?

Let \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) denote the integers modulo \(n\). Determine the second-smallest square-free composite number \(n\) (that is, a product of two distinct primes) for which there exists a unit \(u\) modulo \(n\) such that, for every integer \(k\in\{0,1,2,\dots,231\}\), the map \(x\mapsto ux+kx=(u+k)x\) is a bijection on \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\). Report \(n\). (So there are 232 such maps, one for each \(k\).)

Vera has a row of 49149 coins. Their initial orientations follow a periodic pattern: starting from the left, there are 971 consecutive tails-up coins, then 811 consecutive heads-up coins, and this block repeats cyclically until all 49149 coins are placed (the final block may be truncated). On the first move, she may flip any coin. On each subsequent move, she may only flip a coin adjacent to the coin she flipped on the previous move (we do not consider a coin to be adjacent to itself). Determine the smallest possible number of moves Vera can make to reach a state in which every coin is heads-up.

Consider the square lattice of integer points with coordinates (x, y) where 1 <= x <= 2925 and 1 <= y <= 2925. Select a subset S of these lattice points subject to the following two global constraints:
1) For any two distinct rows y = r1 and y = r2, the average of the x-coordinates of any two points of S in row r1 is never equal to the average of the x-coordinates of any two points of S in row r2. Equivalently, no four selected points can form an isosceles trapezoid whose bases are horizontal (rectangles are considered isosceles trapezoids).
2) For any two distinct columns x = c1 and x = c2, the average of the y-coordinates of any two points of S in column c1 is never equal to the average of the y-coordinates of any two points of S in column c2. Equivalently, no four selected points can form an isosceles trapezoid whose bases are vertical (rectangles are considered isosceles trapezoids).
You are additionally told that in an optimal construction one may assume (and you must implicitly justify by your argument) that no row and no column contains more than three selected points.
What is the maximum possible size of S in terms of 2925?

In a math contest, 149 students are each paired with every other student, forming a complete graph on 149 vertices. Each pair is assigned an integer score from the set 3, 6, 9 with 3 < 6 < 9. The assignment must satisfy: for every group of 7 students, the sum of all pairwise scores among them is at least binomial(7, 2) * 3 + (6 - 3). Among all such assignments, determine the minimum possible average score across all pairs. If this minimum average equals m/n in lowest terms, compute m + n.

In a math contest, 86 integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_86 are arranged in a nondecreasing sequence with a_1 = 4 and a_86 = 61. Each step is bounded: for every i, a_{i+1} - a_i is an integer in [0, 3]. Define F = (a_1^2 + a_2^2 + ... + a_86^2) - 1(a_1a_2 + a_2a_3 + ... + a_{n-1}a_86) - (a_1a_3 + a_2a_4 + ... + a_{n-2}a_86). Find the minimal possible value of F.

Let num_vars be an integer at least 4. Define S_num_vars to be the set of integers s satisfying s >= 4510 for which there exist positive integers a1, a2, ..., a7 with exactly num_vars−1 of them equal (so the num_vars numbers are not all equal), such that a1 + a2 + ... + a7 = s and s divides the sum over i from 1 to num_vars of the product of all a_j with j != i. Compute the sum of the 10 smallest elements of S_num_vars when num_vars = 7.

In a math contest, define F(r, c, k) as the number of black/white colorings of an r×c toroidal chessboard (rows and columns wrap around cyclically) such that: (i) no two black cells are horizontally or vertically adjacent (including wrap-around), and (ii) between any two consecutive rows, no two black cells are diagonally adjacent in either direction (both NE and NW are forbidden, with indices taken modulo r and c). Additionally, the first row contains exactly k black cells. Given c = 5, k = 1, and r ranging from 6 to 7 inclusive, compute S = ∑_{r=6}^7 F(r, 5, 1).

In a math contest, consider a circular binary sequence a_1, a_2, ..., a_27 with indices taken modulo 27, so adjacency includes the wrap-around pair (a_27, a_1). A "reverse order" is an adjacent pair equal to (1,0). You are told that a_1 = 0, that the wrap-around pair (a_27, a_1) is a reverse order, that the sequence has exactly 5 reverse orders around the circle, and that it contains exactly 17 ones in total. Additionally, every maximal run of consecutive 1s has length between 2 and 6 inclusive, and every maximal run of consecutive 0s has length between 2 and 4 inclusive. How many such sequences exist?

In a math contest, there are 16 questions, and each question has exactly two options. A group of students submits answer sheets satisfying both conditions:
- For any two distinct students, the number of questions on which they give the same answer is either 0 or 8.
- For each fixed question, each of the two options is chosen by exactly the same number of students.
Among all such groups, determine the maximum possible number of students.

In a math contest, 270 real numbers x_1, x_2, ..., x_270 are partitioned into three blocks of sizes 79, 74, and 117. For every i in block 1 we have -1/sqrt(8) ≤ x_i ≤ sqrt(8); in block 2, -1/sqrt(6) ≤ x_i ≤ sqrt(6); and in block 3, -1/sqrt(3) ≤ x_i ≤ sqrt(3). The numbers satisfy x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_270 = -53.66715549017769. Let M be the maximal possible value of x_1^{ 16 } + x_2^{ 16 } + ... + x_270^{ 16 }, where 16 is an even integer. Determine the greatest integer less than or equal to M.

In a number theory contest, you are given m distinct positive integers a_1,a_2,\dots,a_m whose full product a_1a_2\cdots a_m has exactly 399 distinct prime divisors. Fix the prime power 389017=73^3. Under the condition that the product of any nonempty subset of \{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_m\} is not a 389017-th power of an integer, determine the maximal possible value of m.

On a circular track of circumference 11832, there are 1479 equally spaced marked points. They are labeled A_1, A_2, ..., A_1479 in some order, each label used exactly once. Bunbun starts at A_1, hops to A_2, then A_3, ..., then A_1479, and finally back to A_1. Every hop is along the shorter arc between the two points (if the chord is a diameter, any semicircle may be used). Over all possible labelings, determine the maximal possible value of the sum of the 5-th powers of the lengths of the 1479 arcs that Bunbun traverses.

Consider pairs (f, g) of functions from the nonnegative integers to the nonnegative integers. Assume f is globally nonincreasing on all n >= 0 and its forward differences d_n = f(n) - f(n+1) form a nonincreasing sequence with each d_n in {0, 1} (so f decreases by exactly 1 at each step for a while, and then becomes constant; under the budget below, that constant must be 0). In addition, the budget constraint holds: f(0) + f(1) + ... + f(211) <= 190. For any choice of 13 nonnegative integers n_1, ..., n_13, we have g(n_1 + ... + n_13) <= f(n_1) + ... + f(n_13). Determine the maximum possible value of g(0) + g(1) + ... + g(211).

In a math contest, 2412 students are arranging chairs into an 321-by-179 rectangular grid. A block of chairs is an axis-aligned rectangular sub-grid. Call a block buffered of radius 8 if its entire Chebyshev-distance 8 neighborhood (i.e., all cells within max-distance r in both row and column) still lies within the overall 321 by 179 grid. Among all possible arrangements of the numbers on the grid (one number per cell), what is the maximum possible number of buffered blocks? Give your answer as a function of 321, 179, and 8.

In a math contest, 3604 students are analyzing a weighted divisibility network. For each integer k with 1721 ≤ k ≤ 3604, choose real numbers x_1, x_2, ..., x_k ∈ [0,1] to maximize

F_k = x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_k − ∑_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ k, i | j, j/i ≤ 3604} x_i x_j.

Let d(k) denote the maximum value of F_k. Compute the sum ∑_{k=1721}^{3604} d(k).

Consider a regular 30-prism. On each lateral rectangular face, draw both face diagonals and let their intersection be a point. Remove all lateral edges of the prism, but keep the base polygon edges. Additionally, connect each such intersection point to the intersection points of the two adjacent lateral faces, forming a cycle of intersection points around the prism. On the resulting graph whose vertices are the 230 base vertices and the 30 intersection points, perform a proper 4-coloring (adjacent vertices cannot share a color). Two colorings are considered the same if one is obtained from the other by a rotation about the prism’s axis. Determine the number of such inequivalent colorings.

Fix an odd integer 3 ≥ 3. A positive integer k is called 3-good if there exist positive integers a and b with a < b such that a^3 = (k a + 1) b + k. Determine the sum of all 3-good integers k that do not exceed 791.

On a regular 150-gon, each vertex starts with exactly 1 coins. In one operation, you select a vertex, take 1 coins from each of its two adjacent vertices, add 1 coins to the selected vertex, and keep the remaining coins you took, which equals 2·1−1. You may perform an operation only if both adjacent vertices have at least 1 coins. You stop when no operation is possible. Let N_max be the maximum total number of coins you can collect, and N_min be the minimum total number of coins you can collect over all valid sequences of operations. Compute 842·N_max + N_min.

On a rectangular 1924×3261 grid, a white piece and a black piece are placed uniformly at random in distinct cells. The white moves first, then the black; both pieces move one cell per turn horizontally or vertically, and for each piece, horizontal and vertical moves must alternate forever. Additionally, white is constrained to begin with a horizontal move, while black is constrained to begin with a vertical move. The players cooperate, choosing directions on each move to try to meet as soon as possible while obeying the alternation rule. Let p = m/n in lowest terms be the probability that there exists a round t such that immediately after the black’s move in round t, the two pieces occupy the same cell. Find m.

On a 3×15 rectangular grid of unit squares, you may place any number of axis-aligned 1×2 dominos. A domino is said to be jammed if, with all other dominos fixed, it cannot slide one unit horizontally or vertically while remaining fully on the board. Determine the minimal possible number of dominos needed to achieve a placement in which every domino is jammed.

Consider a convex 24-gon with positive integer side lengths x_1, x_2, ..., x_24, all congruent to 7 modulo 10. For each integer perimeter m in the interval [208, 668] satisfying m ≡ 24·7 (mod 10) (equivalently, m ≡ 8 (mod 10)), let f(m) be the minimum possible value of the product x_1 x_2 ··· x_24, subject to the strict polygon inequality that the largest side is strictly less than the sum of the other 23 sides. Compute the sum S = ∑ f(m) over all such perimeters m.

In a math contest, 622080000 identical cookies are to be shared among n guests under these rules: (i) each cookie is either left whole or cut into exactly two equal halves; (ii) every guest must receive exactly the same total amount of cookie; (iii) every guest must receive exactly 304633 pieces in total (counting a whole cookie as one piece and each half as one piece). Determine the sum of all positive integers n for which such a distribution is possible.

Consider a cyclic necklace with 240 through 375 beads: for each integer n in this range, take an n-gon whose vertices ("beads") are initially labeled 0. A move consists of choosing two adjacent beads and increasing both their labels by 1. If it is possible, after more than 0 moves, to make all n bead labels equal, define g(n) to be the minimal number of moves needed; otherwise set g(n) = 0. Compute the sum S = sum_{n=240}^{n=375} g(n).

In a math contest, 335 rounds are held. For each positive integer n and real numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n chosen from the interval [-2, 4], let S = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n. Define F(n) to be the maximum possible value of sum_{i=1}^n | (S - 7·a_i)/n - a_i | over all such choices of a_1, ..., a_n. Compute the value of sum_{k=1}^335 k·F(k).

Nonnegative real numbers x_1, x_2, ..., x_46 sum to 1 and satisfy the additional moment constraint sum_{i=1}^46 (2 i - 1)^1 x_i = 72169/1727. For these fixed data, determine the maximal value of S = sum_{i=1}^46 sum_{j=1}^46 ((2 i - 1)^1 / (2 j - 1)^3) x_i x_j. Write the maximum as a reduced fraction m/n and report m+n.

There are 17 distinct cards carrying the consecutive integers from 2 to 18, inclusive, arranged uniformly at random from left to right. Let a_i denote the integer on the i-th card. Consider the event E that for every i = 1, 2, ..., 17, the displacement a_i - i lies between 0 and 3, inclusive. If the probability of E equals a/x in lowest terms, determine a + x.

On the set 18 labeled elements, consider bijections f with f_1(x)=f(x) and f_{k+1}(x)=f(f_k(x)). Suppose f satisfies all of the following: (i) f has no fixed points; (ii) f^36 is the identity mapping; (iii) f^630 fixes exactly 6 elements; and (iv) f is an even permutation. How many such bijections f exist?

There are 459 piles of coins S_1, S_2, ..., S_459. For each prime p listed in the mapping {101: 3, 151: 2, 167: 1, 3: 1, 53: 1, 73: 3, 137: 2, 7: 2, 127: 1, 83: 3, 103: 2, 191: 1, 47: 2, 79: 4, 163: 1, 227: 1, 197: 1, 139: 2, 43: 7, 157: 1, 181: 1, 23: 4, 29: 1, 61: 3}, pile S_k initially contains exactly r_p coins labeled p if and only if p divides k, and contains none of that label otherwise (here r_p is the value associated to p in {101: 3, 151: 2, 167: 1, 3: 1, 53: 1, 73: 3, 137: 2, 7: 2, 127: 1, 83: 3, 103: 2, 191: 1, 47: 2, 79: 4, 163: 1, 227: 1, 197: 1, 139: 2, 43: 7, 157: 1, 181: 1, 23: 4, 29: 1, 61: 3}). An operation selects an ordered triple (i, j, p) satisfying: 1 <= i < j <= 459, p is a prime key of {101: 3, 151: 2, 167: 1, 3: 1, 53: 1, 73: 3, 137: 2, 7: 2, 127: 1, 83: 3, 103: 2, 191: 1, 47: 2, 79: 4, 163: 1, 227: 1, 197: 1, 139: 2, 43: 7, 157: 1, 181: 1, 23: 4, 29: 1, 61: 3}, p divides both i and j, each of S_i and S_j currently has at least one coin labeled p, and the triple (i, j, p) has not been selected before. The operation removes one coin labeled p from each of S_i and S_j. What is the maximum number of operations that can be performed?

You have 21 balls arranged in a row, colored using 5 distinct colors labeled 1 through 5. For each color i (1 ≤ i ≤ 5), you must use exactly the number of balls specified by the vector [1, 6, 3, 1, 10], listed in order of color labels i = 1, 2, ..., 5. Adjacency is restricted by the unordered forbidden-pair set [(4, 5)]: if (u, v) appears in this set, then colors u and v may not be adjacent in either order; in particular, (i, i) forbids two i-colored balls from being consecutive. How many valid arrangements satisfy all the exact-count and adjacency constraints?

In a directed network of 15 labeled nodes 1,2,...,15, for every pair i<j the edge is oriented i→j unless that pair is among a specified set of two-way edges. The two-way edges induce exactly one complete clique on 11 nodes. In addition, there are 3 nodes outside this clique; each of these 3 nodes shares two-way edges with the same fixed set of 3 clique nodes, and there are no two-way edges among the outside nodes. A subset of 4 distinct nodes is called mutually-connected if, using only the edges among those 4 nodes, every node can reach every other node (i.e., the induced subgraph on those nodes is strongly connected). Determine the exact number of mutually-connected 4-subsets.
